en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
14. The Second Story of the Daughter-in-law’s Mansion “O goddess,
you who stand there with such exquisite beauty;”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs—
by what cause do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
Whatever riches arise that are dear to the mind, they come to you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she gave an answer as the fruit of that karma:
"When I was among humans, having become a human being..."
I was a daughter-in-law in my father-in-law's house.
There I saw a stainless bhikkhu,
serene and undisturbed.
With my own hands, full of faith, I gave him a portion;
having given him that lump of rice gruel, I said:
I rejoice in the Nandana grove.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this,
and because of that, it is perfected here for me.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is pleasing to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds; because of that,
my majestic power blazes forth in this way,
and my complexion illuminates all directions."
The second Suṇisā-vimāna, the fourteenth.
